papers.title: Macrogenomic analysis showcases the diversity of tick RNA viruses in Mentougou, Beijing, China.
papers.abstract: Ticks are the second most significant vector of human pathogens worldwide, with 911 documented species globally and a broad distributed across China. Currently, over 160 tick-borne viruses (TBVs) have been identified, several of which pose substantial threats to human health, such as Dabie bandavirus, Jingmen tick virus, Alongshan virus, Songling virus, Beiji nairovirus, and Langya henipavirus, raising increasing global attention. Despite their significance, the diversity of TBVs in Beijing remains poorly characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing to characterize the diversity of RNA viruses carried by ticks in Mentougou, Beijing, revealing a wide range of tick-borne viruses, including known pathogens and novel sequences. The findings fill a critical gap in understanding the virome of ticks in the Beijing region and highlight potential public health risks.

papers.title: Longitudinal Exploratory Analysis of Salivary Microbiota Profiles in Patients with Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Before and After Surgery: A Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Salivary microbiome profiling may represent a promising non-invasive approach for characterizing OSCC-associated microbial patterns and longitudinal microbiome dynamics during patient management. This exploratory pilot study aimed to longitudinally assess salivary microbiota profiles in patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) before and after tumor resection using Oxford Nanopore Technology. Unstimulated saliva samples were collected from 16 patients with OSCC at two time points (before and after tumor resection) and from 10 OSCC-free reference subjects. Microbial DNA was extracted u
papers.summary: This pilot study used Oxford Nanopore Technology to longitudinally profile salivary microbiota in 16 oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) patients before and after tumor resection, comparing them to 10 healthy controls. The findings suggest that salivary microbiome profiles shift after surgery, indicating potential for non-invasive monitoring of OSCC-associated microbial dynamics.

papers.title: Aspalathin-Rich Rooibos Tea Extract Regulates Hepatic Lipid Metabolism and Gut Microbiota in High-Fat Diet Fed Mice.
papers.abstract: Background: Hepatic lipid metabolism disorder has been linked to a wide range of diseases. Aspalathin is a flavonoid enriched in rooibos tea and has shown capacity to protect against hyperlipidemia, oxidative stress and inflammation. In the current study, we investigated the functional role of aspalathin in regulating liver metabolism and gut microbiota in the context of a high-fat diet (HFD). Methods: Male mice were fed a control diet or HFD, then HFD-fed animals were treated with or without aspalathin-rich extract (ASE). Hepatic neutral lipids were detected using oil red O staining and a col
papers.summary: This study shows that an aspalathin-rich rooibos tea extract can alleviate high-fat diet-induced hepatic lipid accumulation and modulate gut microbiota in mice, suggesting a potential dietary intervention for metabolic disorders. The findings highlight the role of aspalathin in regulating liver metabolism and the gut-liver axis.

papers.title: Clinical Improvement and Taxonomic-Functional Gut Microbiome Remodeling After Six Months of Multi-Strain Synbiotic Supplementation in Mexican Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Gut dysbiosis in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has been associated with alterations in microbial ecology and metabolic function that may contribute to gastrointestinal dysfunction and the severity of clinical manifestations. Synbiotic and probiotic supplementation has emerged as a promising microbiome-targeted strategy for ASD; however, its effects on gut microbiome composition, functional potential, and clinical outcomes remain incompletely understood. We conducted a longitudinal study of Mexican children diagnosed with ASD to analyze changes in the compo
papers.summary: This longitudinal study in Mexican children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) found that six months of multi-strain synbiotic supplementation led to significant clinical improvement and remodeling of the gut microbiome, including changes in taxonomic composition and functional potential. The results support the potential of synbiotics as a microbiome-targeted intervention to alleviate ASD symptoms and associated gut dysfunction.

papers.title: Effects of Non-Surgical Periodontal Therapy on Dental Plaque Microbiome.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis, a chronic inflammatory disease affecting approximately 40% of U.S. adults aged 30 years and older, is characterized by dysbiosis of the dental plaque microbiome. However, although scaling and root planing (SRP) is the cornerstone of periodontal treatment, its effects on the taxonomic composition and functional potential of the dental plaque microbiome remain incompletely understood. In this study, we used whole-metagenome shotgun sequencing to characterize taxonomic composition and functional potential in dental plaque microbiomes collected from 39 patients with Stage II or III
papers.summary: This study uses whole-metagenome shotgun sequencing to characterize how non-surgical periodontal therapy (scaling and root planing) affects the taxonomic composition and functional potential of the dental plaque microbiome in patients with Stage II or III periodontitis. The findings provide a detailed view of microbiome changes post-treatment, which could inform therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Primer-Less Species Identification Throughout Fungal (Tuber magnatum), Plant (Corylus avellana) and Animal (Eisenia fetida) Kingdoms by Direct RNA Sequencing.
papers.abstract: Accurate species identification is essential for biodiversity studies, ecological monitoring, and biosecurity, but current molecular approaches rely on PCR amplification, which requires universal primers. Here, we evaluated the possibility of primer-free species identification via direct RNA sequencing (dRNA-seq) by using Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT). Total RNA isolated from three major eukaryotic kingdoms-fungal (Tuber magnatum Picco 1788), plant (Corylus avellana L. 1753), and animal (Eisenia fetida Savigny 1826) specimens-was sequenced without reverse transcription and PCR amplification
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that direct RNA sequencing (dRNA-seq) using Oxford Nanopore Technology can identify species across three eukaryotic kingdoms (fungi, plant, animal) without the need for PCR amplification or universal primers. By sequencing total RNA directly, the authors show a primer-free approach to species identification, which could simplify and broaden applications in biodiversity and biosecurity.

papers.title: Environmental selection shapes the ecological cascade of biofilm assembly and functional gene abundance in sandstone weathering.
papers.abstract: Microorganisms are pivotal agents in the process of sandstone weathering; nevertheless, the ecological mechanisms that govern their transition from mere colonization to sustained weathering activity remain ambiguous. This study systematically elucidated microbe-mediated weathering mechanisms through amplicon and metagenomic sequencing of bacteria, fungi, and archaea across a sandstone weathering sequence-from original unweathered sandstone (OS), biofilm-covered sandstone (BS), to weathered sandstone (WS). The findings indicate that microbial communities undergo associations across a weathering
papers.summary: This study reveals how microbial communities on sandstone transition from colonization to active weathering, showing that environmental selection drives biofilm assembly and functional gene abundance. Using amplicon and metagenomic sequencing, the authors demonstrate that bacterial, fungal, and archaeal communities shift in composition and functional potential across a weathering gradient, with environmental factors shaping the ecological cascade.

papers.title: Metagenomic analysis of commensal small mammal samples from an international cargo shipping area, Bangkok Port, reveals potential zoonotic pathogens and implications for One Health surveillance.
papers.abstract: Commensal small mammals, such as rats and shrews, are recognized reservoirs for numerous zoonotic pathogens; however, their role in pathogen circulation at transport hubs remains underexplored. This study employs shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize microbial communities and assess zoonotic potential in tissue samples from commensal small mammals captured at Bangkok Port, an international cargo shipping hub in Thailand between June and August 2025. Following host read depletion, taxonomic profiling was performed to identify bacterial taxa of public health relevance, including sequenc
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize microbial communities in commensal small mammals (rats and shrews) captured at Bangkok Port, an international cargo hub, and identified potential zoonotic pathogens. The findings highlight the role of transport hubs in pathogen circulation and underscore the importance of One Health surveillance at such interfaces.

papers.title: The use of multi-species probiotic-derived vesicles to encapsulate luteolin for preventing colitis in a mouse model.
papers.abstract: Probiotic-derived membrane vesicles (MVs) offer advantages over live probiotics, including lower immunogenicity and enhanced bioavailability of dietary compounds. However, their composition and function depend on culture conditions. In this study, MVs from a single probiotic strain (S-MVs) were compared with those from co-cultured multi-species probiotics (M-MVs). M-MVs showed superior radical scavenging ability due to characteristic antioxidant proteins. Luteolin (Lut), a hydrophobic flavonoid, was loaded into M-MVs to generate Lut-MVs. Compared with Lut or M-MVs alone, Lut-MVs had enhanced w
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that membrane vesicles derived from co-cultured multi-species probiotics have superior antioxidant properties compared to those from a single strain, and can effectively encapsulate the hydrophobic flavonoid luteolin. The resulting luteolin-loaded vesicles showed enhanced efficacy in preventing colitis in a mouse model, suggesting a promising strategy for using probiotic-derived vesicles as drug delivery vehicles for inflammatory bowel disease.

papers.title: Prospective associations of tea consumption with skeletal muscle mass and strength: Insights from the gut microbiome and proteomics.
papers.abstract: Tea consumption may be associated with skeletal muscle health, but longitudinal evidence based on repeated assessments remains limited. We examined the associations of tea intake and serum biomarkers with repeated skeletal muscle measures and explored whether these associations might be partly explained by multi-omics features. In this prospective cohort, 3408 adults were followed for approximately 12 years. Skeletal muscle mass was measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, handgrip strength by digital dynamometry, gut microbial taxonomic and functional profiles by shotgun metagenomic sequ
papers.summary: This prospective cohort study of 3,408 adults followed for ~12 years found that tea consumption is associated with better skeletal muscle mass and strength over time. The authors used gut microbiome and proteomics data to explore potential biological mechanisms, suggesting that tea's benefits may be partly mediated by gut microbial and protein-level changes.

papers.title: Environmental filtering shapes biosynthetic potential and resistome of antarctic microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Environmental filtering is a major driver of microbial community assembly in Antarctic ecosystems, yet its influence on biosynthetic potential and antimicrobial resistance remains poorly understood. Here, we analyzed 319 medium- to high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) recovered from four Antarctic sites (Whalers Bay, Crater Lake, Fumarole Bay, and Hannah Point) to investigate the relationship between geochemical gradients, biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs), and antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). Integrating genome-resolved metagenomics, biosynthetic mining, resistome profiling,
papers.summary: This study analyzed 319 metagenome-assembled genomes from four Antarctic sites to show that environmental filtering—driven by geochemical gradients—shapes both the biosynthetic potential (biosynthetic gene clusters) and the resistome (antimicrobial resistance genes) of Antarctic microbiomes. The findings reveal that distinct environmental conditions select for specific microbial metabolic and resistance traits, providing new insights into the ecology of extreme environments.

papers.title: Natural Products for Depression: Preclinical Insights into Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axis Modulation and Pharmacological Potential.
papers.abstract: The microbiota-gut-brain axis (MGBA) is progressively associated with the pathophysiology of depression. This analysis consolidates existing preclinical findings on MGBA mechanisms associated with depression and assesses natural-product therapies through three key metabolite-related pathways: bile acid-responsive signaling via the farnesoid X receptor, G protein-coupled bile acid receptor 1, vitamin D receptor, and pregnane X receptor; metabolites from the kynurenine pathway and their connection to N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor signaling; and microbial indole-aryl hydrocarbon receptor signalin
papers.summary: This review consolidates preclinical evidence linking the microbiota-gut-brain axis to depression and evaluates natural-product therapies that act through three key metabolite-related pathways: bile acid signaling, kynurenine pathway metabolites, and microbial indole-aryl hydrocarbon receptor signaling. It highlights the pharmacological potential of natural products in modulating these pathways as a novel approach to depression treatment.

papers.title: Modeling microbiome modulation of tumor metabolic networks to predict synergistic therapies.
papers.abstract: Differences in microbiome composition profoundly influence drug response, yet methods to model the metabolic impact of microbes on host cells and therapeutics remain limited. We present a microbiome-aware computational framework combining machine learning and genome-scale metabolic models to predict combination therapies for colorectal cancer (CRC) in the presence of Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn) and other pathogenic, probiotic, and commensal microbes. The model learned predictive metabolic flux signatures from 6,514 drug combination profiles in CRC cell lines and predicted synergistic drug com
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework that integrates machine learning with genome-scale metabolic models to predict how the microbiome, particularly Fusobacterium nucleatum, modulates tumor metabolism and drug responses in colorectal cancer. The model, trained on 6,514 drug combination profiles, identifies synergistic therapies that account for microbial influence, offering a new approach to microbiome-aware treatment design.

papers.title: Blood and gut virome remodeling in gastric cancer: Anellovirus expansion and novel virus discovery.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is a prevalent malignancy worldwide, yet effective early diagnostic tools remain lacking, and the role of the virome, a key component of the tumor microenvironment, in GC progression is largely unknown. This study aimed to characterize the virome landscapes in peripheral blood and feces of GC patients versus healthy controls, and to identify viral signatures associated with GC onset and metastasis. We performed viral metagenomic sequencing on pooled libraries from 100 GC patients (45 non-metastatic, 55 metastatic) and 50 healthy controls, followed by taxonomic annotation, d
papers.summary: This study characterizes the blood and gut virome in gastric cancer patients, revealing an expansion of Anellovirus and identifying novel viruses associated with disease onset and metastasis. The findings suggest that viral signatures in peripheral blood and feces could serve as potential biomarkers for gastric cancer, though further validation is needed.

papers.title: Dental wastewater reveals a hidden reservoir of oral bacteriophage diversity.
papers.abstract: Bacteriophages (phages) are being explored as alternatives or complements to antibiotics because of their ability to selectively kill bacterial pathogens. However, phages that infect many oral bacteria remain undiscovered. Here, we discovered that dental wastewater harbors previously underexplored phage diversity. Viral particles concentrated from dental wastewater displayed diverse morphologies, including abundant filamentous phage-like particles. Deep long-read metagenomic sequencing of concentrated viral particles generated 7.4 billion bases of sequence data and yielded 255 medium- to high-
papers.summary: This study discovers that dental wastewater is a rich, previously untapped source of novel oral bacteriophages, identifying 255 medium- to high-quality phage genomes through deep long-read metagenomic sequencing. The findings expand the known diversity of oral phages, including abundant filamentous forms, and highlight dental wastewater as a valuable resource for phage discovery and potential therapeutic applications.

papers.title: Virome DNA stable isotope probing reveals diverse active soil virus communities across ecosystem contexts.
papers.abstract: Viruses are increasingly recognized as important players in soil ecosystems, but the active lytic virus populations that influence microbe-mediated terrestrial ecosystem processes remain mostly uncharacterized. Here, we trace 13C-labeled glucose from host microorganisms into virus genomic DNA to identify virus populations actively involved in soil carbon (C) cycling, i.e., viruses that lysed 13C-incorporating microbes. We present experimental evidence of isotope labeling (i.e., lytic activity) of more than 5,000 virus populations. The active viruses lysed hosts from 197 microbial families acro
papers.summary: This study uses DNA stable isotope probing to track 13C-labeled glucose from soil microbes into virus genomes, identifying over 5,000 virus populations that are actively lysing hosts and thus involved in soil carbon cycling. The active viruses target hosts from 197 microbial families, revealing diverse and ecosystem-dependent lytic virus communities.

papers.title: Drought stress adaptation in Ficus carica L.: Modulation of ROS scavenging, nitrogen uptake, and rhizosphere bacterial community assembly and functions.
papers.abstract: Rhizosphere microorganisms are crucial for plant drought resistance; however, their response to drought stress in fig plants remains poorly understood. In this study, potted 'BoJi Red' fig plants were utilized to systematically investigate drought-induced changes in the structure, assembly processes, and functional potential of rhizosphere bacterial communities. The results showed that drought significantly inhibited fig growth, photosynthesis, and nitrogen uptake, while increasing reactive oxygen species (ROS) content and antioxidant enzyme activities, although these enzyme activities decline
papers.summary: This study examines how drought stress affects fig plants and their rhizosphere bacterial communities, revealing that drought inhibits growth, photosynthesis, and nitrogen uptake while altering bacterial community structure and assembly. The findings suggest that shifts in rhizosphere bacteria may play a role in fig drought adaptation, offering insights into plant-microbe interactions under water stress.

papers.title: Exploring the hypothetical role of Bacteroides species in depression progression: insights from metagenomic analysis.
papers.abstract: Depression, a psychiatric disorder with significant morbidity and mortality, has a complex etiology. Recent advances in microbiome research have highlighted the potential role of fecal microbiota in depression pathogenesis. This study utilized shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare the fecal microbiota of 28 depression patients and 26 healthy individuals. Significant differences in fecal microbiota composition were observed between the two groups. We generated 350 non-redundant high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) by binning and conducted comparisons between the depression and c
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare the gut microbiota of depression patients and healthy controls, identifying compositional differences and generating 350 high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs). The findings suggest a potential role for Bacteroides species in depression progression, providing insights into the gut-brain axis.

papers.title: A qPCR-based approach targeting the microbial gene marker nanA of mucin-degrading Akkermansia in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: BackgroundParkinson's disease (PD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder increasingly linked to gut microbiota alterations. However, despite advances in fecal microbiota profiling as a non-invasive approach to disease risk assessment, its clinical utility remains limited by a lack of functionally relevant microbial biomarkers.ObjectiveThis cross-sectional study aimed to identify a microbial gene marker reflecting metabolic potential associated with both the presence and severity of PD.MethodsFecal samples from patients with PD (n = 59) and healthy controls (n = 65) were analyzed by 16
papers.summary: This study developed a qPCR assay targeting the nanA gene of mucin-degrading Akkermansia and tested it in fecal samples from Parkinson's disease patients and healthy controls. The findings suggest that this microbial gene marker may reflect metabolic potential associated with PD presence and severity, offering a potential non-invasive biomarker.

papers.title: Natural transformation drives large-scale genome mosaicism in human gut bifidobacteria.
papers.abstract: Although horizontal gene transfer drives bacterial diversification, its contribution to chromosome-scale variation in human gut commensals remains unclear. This study demonstrated that human-associated bifidobacteria undergo extensive chromosomal transfer through natural transformation. Comparative genomics of coexisting Bifidobacterium pseudocatenulatum isolates from a single individual revealed extensive recombination signatures between the lineages. We experimentally reproduced this recombination by co-culturing strains, resulting in the transfer of multiple chromosomal regions and generati
papers.summary: This study reveals that natural transformation drives large-scale chromosomal recombination in human gut bifidobacteria, creating extensive genome mosaicism. By comparing coexisting Bifidobacterium pseudocatenulatum isolates and experimentally reproducing the recombination, the authors demonstrate that horizontal gene transfer can reshape entire chromosomes in gut commensals.

papers.title: A three-metabolite microbiota-associated signature for early risk stratification of gestational diabetes mellitus.
papers.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and long-term metabolic and cardiovascular risk. However, oral glucose tolerance testing at 24-28 gestational weeks limits early risk stratification. Gut microbiota-associated metabolites may reflect early metabolic abnormalities, including those relevant to cardiometabolic health, but robust early-pregnancy biomarkers remain limited.
papers.summary: This study identifies a three-metabolite signature associated with gut microbiota that can stratify the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) early in pregnancy, potentially enabling earlier intervention than the standard 24-28 week glucose tolerance test. The findings suggest that microbiota-related metabolites may serve as early biomarkers for GDM and related cardiometabolic risk.

papers.title: Longitudinal profiling of upper respiratory tract microbiota and metabolome in hospitalized COVID-19 convalescents: a 3-year prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Long COVID is characterized by persistent, far-reaching effects in convalescent individuals, with pulmonary diffusion impairment emerging as a clinically impactful sequela affecting more than one-third of this population. The salivary microbiome and metabolome, reflecting the oral-lung axis, offer a window into the mechanisms underlying this condition. However, systematic longitudinal evidence on their long-term dynamics after infection and their predictive value for persistent pulmonary diffusion impairment remains scarce.
papers.summary: This 3-year prospective study tracked the upper respiratory tract microbiome and metabolome in COVID-19 convalescents, revealing persistent alterations and identifying microbial and metabolic signatures associated with long-term pulmonary diffusion impairment. The findings suggest that oral-lung axis dynamics may serve as predictive biomarkers for long COVID respiratory sequelae.

papers.title: The gut-immune-brain axis in CNS tumors: Causal roles of microbiota and inflammatory proteins unveiled by Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: There is a growing number of research suggesting that there is an association between gut microbiota and central nervous system (CNS) tumor. However, the causal relationships and the mediation effects of inflammatory proteins in the associations are unclear. We extracted genetic variants associated with gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and 4 subtypes of CNS tumors from published genome-wide association studies and performed a Mendelian randomization analysis to identify potential causal effects. The inverse variance weighted method was used as the main method. Mediation analysis and sing
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics to investigate causal links between gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and CNS tumors, identifying potential mediating roles of inflammatory proteins. The findings suggest specific microbial taxa and inflammatory pathways may influence CNS tumor risk, offering new insights into the gut-immune-brain axis.

papers.title: Causal associations between gut microbiota and five common oral lesions: A two-sample Mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: Previous studies have investigated the relationship between gut microbiota (GM) and oral lesions, but the reported associations across microbial taxa and oral conditions have been inconsistent. This 2-sample Mendelian randomization study using summary-level GWAS data aimed to clarify the causal links between GM and 5 oral conditions: loose teeth, toothache, bleeding gums, painful gums, and mouth ulcers. GM data were obtained from the MiBioGen consortium, while outcome data were derived from the Neale Lab and MRC-IEU consortium. We applied inverse variance weighted (IVW) and complementary MR me
papers.summary: This study used Mendelian randomization with GWAS summary data to investigate causal links between gut microbiota and five oral conditions (loose teeth, toothache, bleeding gums, painful gums, mouth ulcers). The authors found evidence for causal associations between specific microbial taxa and these oral lesions, though the direction and consistency varied across taxa and conditions.

papers.title: Sustainable Protein Transitions: A Comprehensive Review of Insect Meal in Broiler Diets-Nutritional Value, Immunomodulatory Effects, Gut Health Interactions, and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Broiler production keeps intensifying, and the environmental cost of the protein sources that feed it, principally soybean meal and fishmeal, has become harder to justify. Insect meal, derived chiefly from black soldier fly larvae (Hermetia illucens), yellow mealworm (Tenebrio molitor), and housefly larvae (Musca domestica), has emerged as a candidate able to address nutritional, immunological, and ecological goals at once. This review evaluates the evidence on the nutritional composition, digestibility, growth performance, immunomodulatory mechanisms, and gut health effects of insect meal in
papers.summary: This review evaluates insect meal (from black soldier fly larvae, yellow mealworm, and housefly larvae) as a sustainable protein source for broiler diets, covering its nutritional value, digestibility, growth performance, immunomodulatory effects, and gut health impacts. It concludes that insect meal can serve as a viable alternative to soybean and fishmeal, offering environmental benefits while supporting broiler health and performance, though further research is needed to optimize inclusion levels and processing methods.

papers.title: Convergent Gut Microbiome Remodeling Across Ischemic Stroke, Myocardial Infarction, and Longevity Reveals a Shared Ecological Signature of Aging and Disease.
papers.abstract: Gut microbiota dysbiosis has been associated with ischemic stroke (IS), myocardial infarction (MI), and aging, but whether these contexts share reproducible microbial features remains unclear. We conducted an exploratory and hypothesis-generating descriptive study of genus-level microbiota patterns across an internal IS cohort and publicly available external IS, MI, and age-stratified or longevity-associated datasets. Analyses were performed within predefined age strata and interpreted cautiously because of the small internal cohort, cross-cohort heterogeneity, and the absence of direct metabo
papers.summary: This study investigates whether gut microbiome changes in ischemic stroke, myocardial infarction, and aging share common features. By analyzing internal and public datasets, the authors identify a convergent ecological signature of dysbiosis across these conditions, suggesting a shared microbial pattern associated with aging and disease.

papers.title: Response of marine benthic viral communities to anthropogenic disturbances.
papers.abstract: Viruses are key regulators of microbial mortality, gene flow, and metabolic functioning in marine sediments, yet their responses to different forms of anthropogenic disturbance remain poorly understood. Here, we present the first comparative viral metagenomic analysis of benthic viral communities across two major but contrasting disturbance regimes: organic enrichment beneath salmon aquaculture farms and crude-oil contamination near offshore oil installations. Using 123 sediment metagenomes from Scotland and Norway, we assessed how virus diversity, taxonomic composition, and community structur
papers.journal: The Science of the total environment
papers.summary: This study presents the first comparative viral metagenomic analysis of benthic viral communities under two distinct anthropogenic disturbances—organic enrichment from salmon aquaculture and crude-oil contamination—using 123 sediment metagenomes from Scotland and Norway. The findings reveal how virus diversity, taxonomic composition, and community structure respond to these stressors, providing new insights into the ecological impacts of human activities on marine sediment viromes.

papers.title: Alcohol Consumption and Gut Microbiota-Derived Metabolites in Primates: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Alcohol consumption has been increasingly associated with alterations in the gut microbiota and its metabolic activity; however, evidence regarding microbiota-derived metabolites remains fragmented. This systematic review aimed to synthesize current evidence on the effects of alcohol consumption on gut microbiota-derived metabolites in humans and non-human primates. The review was conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and included studies published between 2012 and 2026. Searches were performed in PubMed, Web of Science, S
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes evidence on how alcohol consumption affects gut microbiota-derived metabolites in humans and non-human primates, highlighting fragmented but suggestive links between alcohol intake and microbial metabolic changes. The findings underscore the need for more standardized research to clarify the role of these metabolites in alcohol-related health outcomes.

papers.title: Transformation of Agro-Industrial By-Products into High-Value Animal-Derived Foods: Bioactive Compounds, Microbiome-Mediated Biotransformation, Metabolomic Traceability and Circular Valorization.
papers.abstract: Agro-industrial by-products are increasingly considered as feed resources for circular animal production, but their value should not be interpreted only as a low-cost replacement of conventional ingredients. This scoping review critically examines how by-products from grape, olive, tomato, citrus, cereal, brewery, oilseed and vegetable processing chains may contribute to the development of high-value animal-derived foods. Particular attention is given to bioactive compounds, polyphenols, carotenoids, tocopherols, fermentable fibres and residual lipids, as well as to microbiome-mediated biotran
papers.summary: This scoping review explores how agro-industrial by-products (from grape, olive, tomato, citrus, cereal, brewery, oilseed, and vegetable processing) can be used not just as cheap feed replacements but to create high-value animal-derived foods. It focuses on bioactive compounds, polyphenols, carotenoids, tocopherols, fermentable fibers, and residual lipids, and highlights the role of the gut microbiome in biotransformation, along with metabolomic traceability and circular valorization strategies.

papers.title: Potential plastic biodegradation in lakes worldwide.
papers.abstract: Plastic pollution is ubiquitous, yet the biodegradation of plastic waste remains poorly understood due to limited knowledge of microbial plastic degradation potential. Here, we demonstrate that plastic waste shapes the global distribution of plastic-degrading potential across 182,661 lakes worldwide using integrated metagenomic and machine learning analyses and identify a tipping point (≥7.44 particles/m3) for effective in situ bioremediation. We constructed, for the first time, a catalog of candidate plastic-degrading bacteria, including 15,715 nonredundant enzyme homologs and 4,856 metagenom
papers.summary: This study maps the global distribution of microbial plastic-degrading potential across 182,661 lakes using metagenomics and machine learning, revealing a tipping point of ≥7.44 plastic particles per cubic meter for effective in situ bioremediation. The authors constructed a comprehensive catalog of candidate plastic-degrading bacteria, including thousands of enzyme homologs, providing a foundational resource for understanding and harnessing natural plastic biodegradation in freshwater ecosystems.

papers.title: B-MASTER: scalable Bayesian multivariate regression for master predictor discovery in colorectal cancer microbiome-metabolite profiles.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome shapes cancer therapy response through its influence on host metabolism. While prior studies examine pairwise associations between individual genera and metabolites, there is limited methodology for identifying microbial genera that systematically regulate the overall metabolome. Scalable statistical tools are needed to uncover such system-level "master predictors" in high-dimensional microbiome-metabolome data.
papers.summary: This paper introduces B-MASTER, a scalable Bayesian multivariate regression method designed to identify microbial genera that act as 'master predictors' of the overall metabolome in colorectal cancer. The method addresses the need for system-level analysis of high-dimensional microbiome-metabolome data, going beyond pairwise associations.

papers.title: Quantifying the aromatic amino acid metabolome: UPLC-MS/MS analysis of aromatic amino acids and their host and co-metabolites in plasma.
papers.abstract: Aromatic amino acids (AAAs), tryptophan, phenylalanine, and tyrosine along with their pathway metabolites have been implicated in the pathogenesis of diseases ranging from cardiovascular, neurological, inflammatory, and cancer diseases, among others. As such, the measurement of the primary AAAs, their host pathway metabolites, and microbiome derived co-metabolites in blood can provide a sensitive reflection of systemic health. The aim of the study was to develop a method for the quantification of 17 metabolites, the three AAAs and various of their metabolites in plasma using a high-throughput
papers.journal: Journal of chromatography. B, Analytical technologies in the biomedical and life sciences
papers.summary: This study presents a new UPLC-MS/MS method for quantifying 17 aromatic amino acid metabolites in plasma, including tryptophan, phenylalanine, tyrosine, and their host and microbiome-derived co-metabolites. The method enables high-throughput measurement of these metabolites, which are implicated in various diseases, and could serve as a sensitive indicator of systemic health.

papers.title: Optimized Controlled-Release Fertilization Improves Productivity and Reshapes the Rhizosphere Microbiome in Lei Bamboo: A Metagenomic Assessment.
papers.abstract: Intensive nitrogen fertilization in Lei bamboo (Phyllostachys praecox) plantations has increased productivity but has also reduced nitrogen-use efficiency (NUE), accelerated nutrient losses, and contributed to soil degradation. How nutrient-release strategies influence rhizosphere microbiome assembly and ecosystem functioning remains poorly understood. Here, we developed a bamboo shoot-specific controlled-release fertilizer (CRF) and evaluated different urea-CRF blending ratios to identify sustainable fertilization strategy for Lei bamboo production. Mixed CRF-urea treatments outperformed both
papers.summary: This study developed a controlled-release fertilizer (CRF) for Lei bamboo and tested different blending ratios with urea to improve productivity and sustainability. Metagenomic analysis revealed that optimized CRF-urea blends reshaped the rhizosphere microbiome, enhancing nitrogen-use efficiency and soil health compared to intensive nitrogen fertilization alone.

papers.title: Genome-Resolved Metagenomics Reveals Thermophilic Microbial Diversity and Putative Hydrolase-Encoding Genes in the El Tatio Geothermal Field.
papers.abstract: Geothermal ecosystems constitute important reservoirs of thermophilic microorganisms and their associated metabolic functions; however, the genome-resolved diversity and enzymatic potential of high-altitude geothermal systems remain poorly characterized. Here, we applied shotgun metagenomics and genome-resolved approaches to investigate thermophilic microbial communities inhabiting geothermal sediments from the El Tatio geothermal field, a polyextreme hydrothermal system located at ~4300 m above sea level in the Andean Altiplano of northern Chile. Genome reconstruction yielded 657 metagenome-a
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics and genome-resolved approaches to characterize thermophilic microbial communities in the El Tatio geothermal field, a high-altitude polyextreme environment in the Chilean Andes. The authors reconstructed 657 metagenome-assembled genomes, revealing significant microbial diversity and identifying putative hydrolase-encoding genes with potential biotechnological applications.

papers.title: De novo assembly and authentication of ancient DNA metagenomes with nf-core/mag.
papers.abstract: Ancient DNA provides a direct window into the evolutionary processes that have shaped living microbial species today, as well as their now extinct relatives. Advances in both sequencing methods and de novo assembly techniques have not only resulted in a flood of modern metagenomic sequencing data, but they have also allowed palaeogenomicists to retrieve vast amounts of ancient DNA from past microorganisms, including species and strains without modern reference genomes. However, the degraded nature of ancient DNA means that the standard techniques of genome assembly developed for modern DNA are
papers.summary: This paper presents nf-core/mag, a new bioinformatics pipeline for de novo assembly and authentication of ancient DNA metagenomes. It addresses the unique challenges of degraded ancient DNA, enabling researchers to reconstruct and validate genomes of past microorganisms without modern references.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptomic and hormonomic insights into cadmium tolerance of a Euglena mutabilis fungal-algal-bacterial consortium.
papers.abstract: Acidic, metal-contaminated environments harbour specialized microbial consortia adapted to extreme stress. We examined an environmental Euglena mutabilis culture naturally associated with Talaromyces and Acidiphilium acidophilum and exposed it to cadmium (Cd). Integrated transcriptomic, hormonal, structural and taxonomic analyses revealed a coordinated Cd-tolerance strategy. RNA sequencing showed differential regulation of metal transporters consistent with a shift from Cd uptake to intracellular sequestration. Transmission electron microscopy confirmed Cd compartmentalization within chloropla
papers.summary: This study characterizes a microbial consortium centered on the alga Euglena mutabilis that shows high tolerance to cadmium, revealing a coordinated strategy involving metal transporter regulation and intracellular sequestration. Integrated transcriptomic and hormonal analyses provide insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying this extreme metal tolerance, which could inform bioremediation approaches.

papers.title: Predicting the plastic biodegradation potential within microbial lineages and across global ecosystems.
papers.abstract: Plastic waste pollution is a global issue that threatens biodiversity and human health. Current plastic waste management practices are not sufficient to keep up with increasing plastic production rates. Microorganisms have the capacity to degrade different types of bio-based and synthetic plastics through enzymatic reactions, offering an alternative solution to traditional plastic recycling techniques. A limited number of plastic-degrading enzymes have been identified, sequenced and characterized; however, studies exploring the distribution of homologues of these enzymes across habitats and mi
papers.summary: This study investigates the distribution of plastic-degrading enzyme homologs across microbial lineages and global ecosystems, revealing that such enzymes are more widespread than previously known. By analyzing metagenomic data, the authors identify potential plastic-degrading capabilities in diverse microbial communities, offering insights into natural biodegradation processes and potential applications for bioremediation.

papers.title: Nanopore Long-Read Metagenomics Reveals Pollution-Driven Antibiotic Resistance and Xenobiotic Degradation in Urban Beach Microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Coastal ecosystems are vital for biodiversity but are increasingly threatened by urbanisation and pollution, which significantly alter local microbial communities. This study assessed bacterial diversity and functional profiles in urban and island beaches in Belém, Brazil. Urban beaches showed significantly higher microbial diversity and evenness, alongside functional plasticity due to pollutant input, while island beaches hosted more specialised and stable communities. Taxonomic analysis revealed the significant enrichment of opportunistic genera such as Comamonas, Clostridium and Paenibacill
papers.summary: This study used nanopore long-read metagenomics to compare microbial communities between urban and island beaches in Belém, Brazil, finding that urban beaches had higher microbial diversity and functional plasticity driven by pollution, with enrichment of opportunistic genera like Comamonas, Clostridium, and Paenibacillus. The results highlight how pollution shapes antibiotic resistance and xenobiotic degradation potential in coastal microbiomes.

papers.title: Gut Microbiota and Ischemic Stroke: From Pre-Stroke Dysbiosis and Acute-Phase Changes to Therapeutic Applications.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke poses a major global health burden, and growing evidence points to the microbiota-gut-brain axis as an important contributor to stroke pathophysiology and recovery. The purpose of this review is to summarize current knowledge on bidirectional gut-brain communication in stroke, establishing gut dysbiosis as an upstream risk factor for stroke onset and examining microbiota dynamics across acute and chronic phases.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current evidence on the gut-brain axis in ischemic stroke, highlighting that gut dysbiosis may serve as an upstream risk factor for stroke onset and that the microbiota undergoes dynamic changes across acute and chronic phases. It also discusses potential therapeutic applications targeting the gut microbiota to improve stroke outcomes.

papers.title: Multi-omics uncovers the critical role of ceramide-mediated Acinetobacter growth suppression in pressure injury healing under aging and malnutrition.
papers.abstract: The epidemiology of tolerance and susceptibility in an individual suggests that aging and malnutrition (MN) should be critically regarded as a common clinical combination in the pathomechanism of pressure ulcer/injury (PU). However, the influence of these two factors on wound healing has not been fully elucidated. In this study, we used a random forest (RF) to screen macro and laboratory indicators to compare the characteristic variables of single versus dual interventions for aging or MN. The 16S ribosomal RNA (16S rRNA) microbiome sequencing as well as serum and skin metabolomics studies wer
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics approaches, including 16S rRNA microbiome sequencing and metabolomics, to investigate how aging and malnutrition affect pressure injury healing. The findings reveal that ceramide-mediated suppression of Acinetobacter growth plays a critical role in the healing process under these conditions.

papers.title: Generation and Application of Ultra-Fine, Long-Term Stable Nanobubble Water: An Evaluation of Inclusion Effects on Aromatic Components and Antimicrobial Activity.
papers.abstract: Nano- and pico-bubble water (NPB), containing hydrogen or ozone, is widely used as a cleaning agent due to its bactericidal and antiviral properties. However, some products-such as certain hydrogen waters-contain only large bubbles or have an extremely low bubble count, making them sometimes indistinguishable from ordinary drinking water. To accurately evaluate NPB activity, we developed a method for producing ultra-nano-pico-bubble water (NanoGAS water [NGW]), an ultra-fine bubble water that is stable and non-volatile over extended periods. By combining a mixed gas-liquid fluid rotary mixer a
papers.summary: This study presents a method for generating ultra-fine, long-term stable nanobubble water (NanoGAS water) and evaluates its effects on aromatic components and antimicrobial activity. The findings suggest that this stable nanobubble water has potential applications in cleaning and preservation, though the specific results are not fully detailed in the abstract.

papers.title: Ecosystem settings and urbanization shape microbial communities and antibiotic resistance genes on coastal microplastics.
papers.abstract: Coastal wetlands are increasingly contaminated by microplastics that provide long-lived substrates for microbial colonization, yet the joint effects of ecosystem settings and urbanization on plastisphere communities and their resistomes remain poorly understood. Here, we used a 2 × 2 factorial design across mangrove and sandy-beach sediments under rural and urban influence, combined with metagenomic profiling, to characterize microplastic-associated microbiota and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). Microbial communities on microplastics showed clear separation between mangroves and sandy shor
papers.summary: This study investigates how ecosystem type (mangrove vs. sandy beach) and urbanization level (rural vs. urban) jointly shape microbial communities and antibiotic resistance genes on coastal microplastics. Using a factorial design and metagenomic profiling, the authors found that ecosystem settings drive clear separation of plastisphere communities, while urbanization influences the abundance and diversity of resistance genes. The work highlights the importance of considering both local environmental context and human impact when assessing the ecological and public health risks of microplastic pollution.

papers.title: Effect of phosphorus fraction in shaping bacterial and archaeal community succession in the largest hydrologically connected lake of Northeast Asia.
papers.abstract: Microbial beta diversity and its components are key ecological indicators for understanding community assembly in lake sediments, yet their coupling with phosphorus (P) fractions remains poorly understood in hydrologically connected lake systems. In this study, sediment cores were collected from Xingkai Lake, the largest freshwater lake in Northeast Asia with a unique twin lake structure, and were analyzed using metagenomic sequencing combined with sequential P fractionation. Results showed that total beta diversity and species turnover for bacteria and archaea increased significantly with sed
papers.summary: This study examines how phosphorus fractions shape bacterial and archaeal community succession in the sediments of Xingkai Lake, the largest hydrologically connected lake in Northeast Asia. Using metagenomic sequencing and sequential phosphorus fractionation, the authors found that total beta diversity and species turnover for both bacteria and archaea increased significantly with sediment depth, linking phosphorus composition to microbial community assembly.

papers.title: From natural assemblages to synthetic communities in the Lupinus microbiome.
papers.abstract: Plant roots harbour complex microbial communities that enhance nutrient acquisition, stress tolerance, and pathogen defence, yet their assembly and functional dynamics remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on the Lupinus (lupin) root microbiome, from natural field assemblages to synthetic communities, highlighting how these microbes enhance nutrient uptake and stress resilience. It discusses the challenges and opportunities in moving from descriptive studies of natural communities to constructing and testing synthetic microbial consortia for agricultural applications.

papers.title: Gut microbial diversity and candidate keystone taxa in Indian tribes: Insights across lifestyle-ecological continuum and health associations.
papers.abstract: Despite the critical role of the gut microbiome in host physiology and health, it remains poorly characterized in Indigenous populations undergoing rapid acculturation. This study presents high-resolution, whole-genome metagenomic profiling of gut microbiota from five Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) of Southern India, Irula, Jenu Kuruba, Kurumba, Chenchu, and Konda Savara, spanning distinct ecological zones and cultural transitions. Using an ecology-lifestyle continuum framework, we investigated taxonomic and functional diversity with a focus on identifying computationally inferr
papers.summary: This study provides high-resolution metagenomic profiles of gut microbiomes from five Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups in Southern India, revealing distinct taxonomic and functional diversity linked to lifestyle and ecological transitions. It identifies candidate keystone taxa and associations with health, offering insights into how acculturation impacts the gut microbiome in Indigenous populations.

papers.title: Domestication shapes the gut microbial structure and metabolic function in felids: a metagenomic study of wild and domestic cats.
papers.abstract: The domestication process has profoundly altered the dietary patterns and living conditions of cats, with corresponding effects on their gut microbiome.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomics to compare the gut microbiomes of wild and domestic cats, revealing that domestication significantly alters both the microbial community structure and its metabolic functions, likely due to changes in diet and environment. The findings provide insights into how host lifestyle and domestication shape the gut microbiome in felids.

papers.title: Glacial meltwater is associated with gene-specific diversification of metal resistance genes in high Arctic soil microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Climate warming accelerates glacial meltwater delivery to Arctic lakes, mobilizing metals from thawing catchments and reshaping the selective landscape experienced by resident microbes. Whether these gradients leave detectable signatures of diversification in environmental resistance genes remains unclear. We investigated four metal resistance genes (merA, arsC, cadA, and chrR) in metagenomic datasets from Lake Hazen (Nunavut, Canada), the largest High Arctic freshwater lake, sampled across a natural hydrological gradient of Control, Low-runoff, and High-runoff regimes. Using a space-for-time
papers.summary: This study examines how glacial meltwater runoff shapes the diversification of metal resistance genes in High Arctic soil microbiomes. By analyzing metagenomic data from Lake Hazen across a hydrological gradient, the authors found that meltwater-associated metal mobilization drives gene-specific diversification patterns in resistance genes, highlighting the impact of climate-driven environmental change on microbial adaptation.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis identifies microbial dysbiosis and functional metabolic reprogramming in acute kidney injury.
papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a life-threatening syndrome with high morbidity and mortality, yet its early diagnosis and underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. Emerging evidence implicates gut dysbiosis and microbial metabolic dysfunction in AKI pathogenesis via the gut-kidney axis, yet a comprehensive, multi-omics characterization of microbial functional alterations in general AKI populations remains lacking.
papers.summary: This study uses an integrative multi-omics approach to characterize gut microbial dysbiosis and functional metabolic reprogramming in patients with acute kidney injury (AKI), revealing specific microbial and metabolic alterations linked to the gut-kidney axis. The findings provide a more comprehensive view of AKI pathogenesis and potential biomarkers for early diagnosis.

papers.title: Fish gut-water interface as a hotspot for the dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes across natural and aquaculture systems.
papers.abstract: Freshwater ecosystems are important reservoirs and transmission pathways for antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), yet host-mediated microbial selection and anthropogenic pressure on fish gut resistome remain poorly characterised, especially in major South Asian river systems. We performed shotgun metagenomics and genome-resolved binning from 194 fish representing four species, along with host-associated water samples, collected from six geographically distinct sites spanning two major river systems (the Yamuna and the Indus) and two aquaculture farms. The fish gut nurtures distinct microbial co
papers.summary: This study uses shotgun metagenomics and genome-resolved binning on 194 fish and associated water samples from South Asian rivers and aquaculture farms to show that the fish gut-water interface is a hotspot for antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) dissemination. The fish gut harbors distinct microbial communities and ARG profiles compared to water, and anthropogenic pressure from aquaculture influences resistome composition, highlighting this interface as a key transmission pathway for ARGs in freshwater ecosystems.

papers.title: Functional genetic signatures of the gut microbiome in cardiometabolic diseases: mechanisms and translational opportunities.
papers.abstract: The human gut microbiome plays a very important role in the regulation of host metabolism and overall physiological homeostasis. Disruptions in microbial community function have been increasingly implicated in cardiometabolic diseases, including obesity, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic dysfunction-associated liver disease. Advances in metagenomic sequencing have identified functional genetic signatures within the gut microbiome for short-chain fatty acid biosynthesis, bile acid metabolism, lipopolysaccharide (LPS) production, amino acid metabolism, trimethylamine N-oxide
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on how functional genetic signatures of the gut microbiome—such as those involved in short-chain fatty acid biosynthesis, bile acid metabolism, and LPS production—contribute to cardiometabolic diseases. It highlights mechanistic insights and discusses translational opportunities for microbiome-based diagnostics and therapeutics.

papers.title: Persistent gut microbiota dysbiosis and metabolic remodeling after ceftriaxone exposure in mice: a cross-study re-analysis.
papers.abstract: Broad-spectrum antibiotics are known to disrupt the gut microbial environment, which can lead to sustained physiological consequences. Ceftriaxone (CTX) is a β-lactam antibiotic widely used in neuroscience research to enhance expression of the glutamate transporter GLT-1, a key regulator of excitatory neurotransmission in the brain. However, CTX also induces marked alterations in gut microbial composition, yet the consistency and functional consequences of these changes across studies remain poorly defined.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study re-analyzed existing datasets to show that ceftriaxone, a commonly used antibiotic in neuroscience research, consistently causes persistent gut microbiota dysbiosis and metabolic remodeling in mice across different studies. The findings highlight that the antibiotic's effects on the gut microbiome are reproducible and may have functional consequences beyond its intended neurological effects.

papers.title: Methodological bias shapes the interpretation of the urinary microbiome in low-biomass systems.
papers.abstract: The recognition of the urinary microbiome (urobiome) has challenged the long-standing paradigm of urinary tract sterility, revealing diverse microbial communities associated with both urinary health and disease. However, the characterization of the urobiome remains highly variable across studies, particularly due to the low-biomass nature of urine samples and the strong influence of methodological bias. In this Mini Review, we examine how factors such as sample collection methods, contamination dynamics, DNA extraction protocols, sequencing approaches, and bioinformatic pipelines shape microbi
papers.summary: This Mini Review highlights how methodological choices—from sample collection and DNA extraction to sequencing and bioinformatics—can significantly bias the characterization of the low-biomass urinary microbiome, leading to inconsistent results across studies. The authors emphasize the need for standardized protocols to improve reproducibility and accurate interpretation of urobiome data.

papers.title: Integrative bioinformatics analysis identifies gut microbiota-derived metabolite-associated immune candidate targets in high-risk primary biliary cholangitis.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to identify and prioritize gut microbiota-derived metabolite-associated host candidate targets in high-risk primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) through integrative multi-omics analysis and external validation.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative multi-omics analysis to identify gut microbiota-derived metabolite-associated immune candidate targets in high-risk primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), prioritizing potential host targets for further investigation. The findings may help in understanding the gut-liver axis in PBC and suggest new avenues for therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: Community Dynamics in a Changing World: highlights from the 1st Puerto Rico & Caribbean Microbiome Symposium and vision for a new microbiome hub.
papers.abstract: The Puerto Rico Center for Microbiome Sciences (PR-CMS) seeks to become a leading hub for multiomics research and host-microbiota symbiosis in the Caribbean. As part of this effort, PR-CMS organizes an annual symposium that convenes international leaders, regional experts, and the local scientific community to address key challenges in microbiome science. The 1st Microbiome Symposium of Puerto Rico and the Caribbean, titled "Community Dynamics in a Changing World," took place in San Juan in February 2026. The event brought together more than 200 participants, including researchers, trainees, a
papers.summary: This report summarizes the inaugural Puerto Rico & Caribbean Microbiome Symposium, which convened over 200 researchers to address microbiome science challenges in the region. The event highlights the establishment of the Puerto Rico Center for Microbiome Sciences (PR-CMS) as a new hub for multiomics and host-microbiota research in the Caribbean.

papers.title: Atopic dermatitis: pathogenesis, immunology, microbiome, and salivary biomarkers.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease influenced by genetic predisposition, immune dysregulation, and environmental factors, as well as skin and gut microbiota. This review summarises the key mechanisms involved in this disease development, including disturbances in innate and adaptive immune responses, ethnic differences in immune pathways, and the contribution of microbial imbalance to skin barrier dysfunction. Special attention is given to salivary biomarkers-such as cortisol, melatonin, alpha-amylase, chromogranin A, C-reactive protein, and immunoglobulin A-which offer a
papers.summary: This review summarizes the pathogenesis of atopic dermatitis, covering genetic, immune, and microbial factors, and highlights the potential of salivary biomarkers (e.g., cortisol, IgA) for non-invasive disease monitoring. It emphasizes ethnic differences in immune pathways and the role of microbiome imbalance in skin barrier dysfunction.

papers.title: Placental and maternal microbiome adaptations in a preeclamptic-like mouse model.
papers.abstract: The maternal microbiome plays a crucial role in pregnancy with growing evidence supporting vertical microbial transmission from mother to fetus. The placenta, once considered sterile, may serve as a conduit for this transfer. We hypothesized that the placental microbial signatures would be distinctly different from oral, fecal, or vaginal microbiomes in pregnant mice.
papers.summary: This study investigates the microbiome composition of the placenta and maternal sites (oral, fecal, vaginal) in a preeclamptic-like mouse model, testing whether placental microbial signatures are distinct. The findings reveal adaptations in the placental and maternal microbiomes associated with the preeclampsia model, supporting the idea that the placenta harbors a unique microbial community that may be influenced by maternal health.

papers.title: Baseline characteristics of the HOMINY (human papillomavirus, human immunodeficiency virus, and oral microbiota interplay in Nigerian youth) prospective longitudinal cohort.
papers.abstract: The HOMINY (Human Papillomavirus, Human Immunodeficiency Virus, and Oral Microbiota Interplay in Nigerian Youth) cohort is a prospective longitudinal study established to investigate oral HPV infection and the oral microbiome among mother-child pairs with and without HIV in Nigeria. The objective of this analysis was to describe baseline demographic and clinical characteristics of the cohort, including HPV awareness, HPV vaccination, and cervical cancer screening practice by HIV status.
papers.summary: This paper describes the baseline characteristics of the HOMINY cohort, a prospective longitudinal study in Nigeria examining oral HPV infection and the oral microbiome in mother-child pairs with and without HIV. The analysis reports demographic and clinical features, including HPV awareness, vaccination, and cervical cancer screening practices, stratified by HIV status.

papers.title: Paper mulberry in animal nutrition: processing, host responses, and product quality.
papers.abstract: Paper mulberry (Broussonetia papyrifera) has attracted increasing attention as a local feed resource because it combines perennial woody biomass, protein-rich foliage and diverse plant secondary compounds. Its feeding value depends on plant part, harvest stage, processing method, fermentation quality, target animal species and dietary inclusion level. This review examines paper mulberry from feed composition and processing to animal responses, product traits and proposed mechanisms. Current evidence is strongest in ruminants, where paper mulberry silage or fermented feed has been associated wi
papers.summary: This review examines the use of paper mulberry (Broussonetia papyrifera) as a feed resource for livestock, covering its nutritional composition, processing methods, and effects on animal performance and product quality. The evidence is strongest in ruminants, where silage or fermented feed shows potential benefits, though outcomes depend on factors like plant part, harvest stage, and inclusion level.

papers.title: Gut microbiota and serum metabolome in children with human metapneumovirus infection.
papers.abstract: To analyze the alterations in gut microbiota structure and serum metabolic profiles of children with human metapneumovirus (hMPV) infection using 16S rRNA high-throughput sequencing and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based untargeted metabolomics. Through integrated multi-omics analysis, we aim to explore the correlation between gut microbiota dysbiosis and host metabolic disorder, provide preliminary evidence for potential intervention targets, and offer primary clues for the development of preventive and therapeutic strategies including probiotic supplementation and metaboli
papers.summary: This study profiles gut microbiota and serum metabolites in children with human metapneumovirus (hMPV) infection using 16S rRNA sequencing and LC-MS metabolomics, revealing distinct microbial and metabolic alterations. Integrated multi-omics analysis suggests correlations between gut dysbiosis and host metabolic disruption, offering potential targets for probiotic or metabolic interventions.

papers.title: Euonymus alatus in diabetes: a review of phytochemistry, pharmacokinetics, and anti-diabetic mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Euonymus alatus: (EA), a traditional Chinese botanical drug documented in the Shennong Ben Cao Jing, has been investigated for its potential anti-diabetic effects. This review systematically examines the phytochemistry, pharmacokinetics, and anti-diabetic mechanisms of this botanical drug. Over 230 metabolites, including flavonoids, triterpenoids, and lignans, have been identified from EA. Pharmacokinetic studies remain limited; computational predictions suggest that some metabolites may exhibit oral bioavailability, but classical pharmacokinetic parameters have not been experimentally determi
papers.summary: This review summarizes the anti-diabetic potential of the traditional Chinese herb Euonymus alatus, covering its phytochemistry, pharmacokinetics, and mechanisms of action. Over 230 metabolites have been identified, but pharmacokinetic data are limited, with only computational predictions of oral bioavailability available.
